en: The Questions of King Milinda,
Great Chapter 1:
The Question on Designation (Paññatti-pañha)

Then King Milinda approached the Venerable Nāgasena; having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Venerable Nāgasena. After exchanging polite and courteous conversation, he sat down to one side.
The Venerable Nāgasena, by means of his own welcoming greetings, won over the mind of King Milinda.
Then King Milinda said this to the Venerable Nāgasena:
“How are you known, venerable sir? What is your name, bhante?
“I am known as ‘Nāgasena,’ great king; my fellow celibates address me as ‘Nāgasena,’ great king.
Moreover, it is the parents who give the name—whether ‘Nāgasena,’ or ‘Sūrasena,’ or ‘Vīrasena.’”
“Or ‘Sīhasena’—rather, Great King, this ‘Nāgasena’ is a designation, a convention, a description, a common usage, a mere name;
herein no person (puggala) is found.
Then King Milinda spoke thus:
“Listen, sirs, you five hundred Yonakas and eighty thousand bhikkhus:
this Nāgasena has said, ‘No person is found here. Is it indeed proper to approve of that?
Then King Milinda said this to the Venerable Nāgasena:
“If, venerable Nāgasena, a person is not found, who then gives you robes, alms-food, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick?
Who partakes of them? Who guards morality? Who devotes himself to meditation? Who realizes the paths, the fruits, and Nibbāna?
Who kills a living being? Who takes what is not given? Who engages in sexual misconduct?”
Mūsā said: "Who drinks liquor? Who commits an act of immediate retribution (*pañcānantariya-kamma*)?
Therefore, there is no wholesome, there is no unwholesome, there is no doer or instigator of wholesome or unwholesome deeds, and there is no fruit or result of well-done or ill-done deeds.
Venerable Nāgasena, if one who kills you does not exist, then for him too there is no taking of life."
“Venerable Nāgasena, you too have no teacher, no preceptor, and no higher ordination.
As for what you said—that your fellow celibates address you as ‘Nāgasena’—who here is Nāgasena?
Is it, venerable sir, the hair that is Nāgasena?”
“No indeed, Great King.
“Is the hair Nāgasena?
“No indeed, Great King.”
“Nails … teeth … skin …”
flesh … sinew … bone …
bone marrow … kidney … heart …
the liver … the midriff … the spleen …
the lungs … the intestines … the mesentery …
the undigested food in the stomach … feces … bile …
Phlegm … pus … blood …
sweat … fear … tears …
Fat … saliva … snot …
“Is the synovial fluid … the urine … up to … the brain matter in the head Nāgasena? [he asked].
“No indeed, Great King.
“But what then, Bhante, is form Nāgasena?
“No indeed, Great King.”
“Is feeling Nāgasena?
“No, great king.
“Is perception Nāgasena?”
“No indeed, Great King.
“Are volitional formations Nāgasena?
“No indeed, Great King.”
“Is consciousness Nāgasena?
“No, great king.
“But, venerable sir, are form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness Nāgasena?”
“No indeed, Great King.
“But then, venerable sir, is Nāgasena something other than form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness?
“No indeed, Great King.”
“Venerable sir, though I have asked him again and again, I do not see Nāgasena.
Is it merely the word ‘Nāgasena,’ venerable sir, that is Nāgasena?
“No, great king,” [he replied].
“But who here is Nāgasena? You, venerable sir, are speaking a falsehood, a lie; there is no Nāgasena.
Then the Venerable Nāgasena said this to King Milinda:
“You, Great King, are a delicate Khattiya, extremely refined. At this time of midday, Great King...”
“Having been crushed by that ground which was hot, with sand that was coarse and gravel-stones, as you walked on foot,
your feet were wounded, your body grew weary, your mind was distressed, and a bodily consciousness accompanied by suffering arose.
Did you indeed come on foot, or rather by vehicle?”
“I do not come on foot, venerable sir; I have come by chariot.
“If you have come by chariot, great king, describe the chariot to me. Now, great king, is the pole the chariot?
“No, venerable sir.”
“Is the axle the chariot?
“No, venerable sir.
“Are the wheels the chariot?”
“No, venerable sir.
“Is the chariot-fender the chariot?
“No, venerable sir.”
“Is the chariot-pole the chariot?
“No, venerable sir.
“Is the yoke the chariot?”
“No indeed, Bhante.
“Are the reins the chariot?
“No indeed, Bhante.”
“Is the goad-stick the chariot?
“No, venerable sir.
“Then, great king, are the pole, the axle, the wheels, the chariot-fender, the chariot-shaft, the yoke, the reins, and the goad-stick the chariot?”
“No, venerable sir.
“But what then, great king, apart from the pole, the axle, the wheels, the chariot-fender, the chariot-shaft, the yoke, the reins, and the goad—is there a chariot?
“No, venerable sir.”
“Even though I have been searching for it again and again, O Great King, I do not see the chariot.
Is it, O Great King, that the mere sound of ‘chariot’ is the chariot?
“Certainly not, venerable sir.”
“But what chariot is there here? You are speaking falsely, Great King; you are uttering a lie. There is no chariot.
You, Great King, are the supreme king over the whole of Jambudīpa; out of fear of whom do you speak such a falsehood?
Let these five hundred Yonakas and eighty thousand bhikkhus hear from me: this King Milinda says thus.”

“If you say, ‘I have come by chariot,’ and if you, Great King, have indeed come by chariot, yet when asked, ‘Tell me about your chariot,’ you do not provide an account of it—is that a fit thing to be approved?
When this was said, the five hundred Yonakas applauded the Venerable Nāgasena and said to King Milinda:
“Now, Great King, speak if you are able.”
Then King Milinda said this to the Venerable Nāgasena: "Venerable Nāgasena,
I am not speaking falsely when I say that it is in dependence upon the pole, in dependence upon the axle, in dependence upon the wheels,
in dependence upon the chariot-fender, and in dependence upon the chariot-pole, that there is the designation, the convention, 'chariot'."
“Designation, conventional usage, and mere name proceed.
“It is good, Great King, that you understand the chariot;
even so, Great King, for me too, depending on the head-hairs and depending on the body-hairs … [and so on] … and depending on the brain in the skull.”
Dependent upon form, dependent upon feeling, dependent upon perception, dependent upon volitional formations, and dependent upon consciousness,
the designation, the convention, the description, the usage, and the mere name "Nāgasena" occurs;
however, in the ultimate sense, no person is found here.
This was indeed spoken, Great King, by the bhikkhunī Vajirā in the presence of the Blessed One:
"Just as it is only through the assembly of parts that there is the designation 'chariot,' so too..."
“Thus, when the aggregates exist, there is the conventional designation ‘a being.
“It is wonderful, venerable Nāgasena! It is marvelous, venerable Nāgasena! Your responses to these questions are most brilliant.”
“Having been answered thus, if the Buddha were present, he would give his approval, saying: ‘Excellent, excellent, Nāgasena!
These answers to your questions are most wonderful.
This is the first question on definitions.
